discoveryHook.scenario: Multi-step inequalities look complicated, but they're just a puzzle with a few more layers. You already know how to simplify expressions and use inverse operations. Now you'll combine those skills, keeping an eye out for the one twist: multiplying or dividing by a negative flips the inequality!

confusionCorner.body: When solving $ 2v - 4 \ge 8 $, we add 4 (no reversal) and divide by 2 (positive, no reversal). Only when we multiply or divide by a negative, like in $ \frac{y}{-6} < 2 $, do we reverse the symbol.
confusionCorner.title: Reverse Only for Multiplication/Division by a Negative

blocks.title: Solving Multi-Step Inequalities

questions.prompt: To solve $ \frac{y}{-6} + 7 < 9 $, the first step is to subtract ___ from both sides.
hints: Look at the constant added to the fraction.
To undo division, multiply by the denominator.
questions.prompt: After subtracting 7 from $ \frac{y}{-6} + 7 < 9 $, what operation must you perform next?

hints: The rule says reverse only for negative multiplier/divisor.
Check the sign of the number you divide by.
questions.prompt: When solving $ 2v - 4 \ge 8 $, why don't we reverse the inequality symbol when dividing by 2?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Because 2 is positive; we only reverse for negative numbers.

examples.title: A – Negative Denominator
steps: Subtract 7 from both sides: $ \frac{y}{-6} < 2 $.
Multiply both sides by -6 and reverse < to >: $ y > -12 $.
Graph: open circle at -12, shade right.

examples.title: B – Positive Coefficient, Two Steps
examples.peerPrompt: Explain to a partner: Why do we add 4 before dividing by 2? And why don't we reverse the symbol?
steps: Add 4 to both sides: $ 2v \ge 12 $.
Divide both sides by 2 (positive, keep symbol): $ v \ge 6 $.
Graph: closed circle at 6, shade right.
Subtract 8 from both sides: $ -9c \ge -36 $.
Divide by -9 and reverse $ \ge $ to $ \le $: $ c \le 4 $.
Graph: closed circle at 4, shade left.
examples.title: C – Variable on Right, Simplify First

formulaCard.title: Solving $ \frac{y}{-6} + 7 < 9 $
notes: Subtract $ a $ first, then multiply by the denominator.
If the denominator is negative, reverse the inequality symbol.

explanation: A [[kw:multi-step inequality]] requires more than one operation to isolate the variable.
Simplify each side first: use the Distributive Property and [[imp:combine like terms]] if needed.
Then use inverse operations to isolate the variable, just like solving multi-step equations.
[[imp:Reverse the inequality symbol]] whenever you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number.
Always graph the solution on a number line to visualize the set of answers.

teacherCues: Write '2v - 4 ≥ 8' on the board. Ask: 'What two operations are applied to v? How do we undo them?'
Remind students: The process is just like multi-step equations, but we must reverse the inequality symbol if we multiply or divide by a negative number.

blocks.title: Variables on Both Sides

examples.title: A – Basic Collecting
steps: Add 5 to both sides: $ 6x < 2x + 16 $.
Subtract $ 2x $: $ 4x < 16 $.
Divide by 4: $ x < 4 $. Graph: open circle at 4, shade left.

examples.peerPrompt: Explain to a partner: After moving terms, if the coefficient of the variable is negative, what must you do?
examples.title: B – Negative Coefficient After Collecting
steps: Divide by -5 and reverse < to >: $ d > -2 $.
Graph: open circle at -2, shade right.

examples.title: C – Simplify Before Collecting
steps: Combine like terms on left: $ 3g - 4 \le -3 + 3g $.
Subtract $ 3g $ from both sides: $ -4 \le -3 $, which is true.
The inequality is true for all real numbers. Graph: entire number line shaded.

confusionCorner.title: Don't Forget to Collect on One Side
confusionCorner.body: When you have variable terms on both sides, you must collect them. But don't forget the inequality properties: if you end with a negative coefficient, you'll reverse the sign when dividing.

discoveryHook.scenario: When an inequality has variables on both sides, it's like a tug-of-war with an unknown number of people on each team. You need to bring all the variable terms to one side to see who wins — without breaking the rules of inequality!

questions.prompt: To solve $ 6x - 5 < 2x + 11 $, after adding 5, you should subtract ___ from both sides.
hints: Look at the variable term on the right.
You want all x terms on the left.
Collect x terms on one side, constants on the other.
questions.prompt: Solve $ 5x - 12 \le 3x - 4 $. What is the solution? (e.g., x <= 4)
In solving $ -2d - 2 < 3d + 8 $, what operation causes the inequality symbol to reverse?

explanation: An inequality with variables on both sides is solved similarly to an equation with variables on both sides.
First, simplify each side if necessary.
Then [[imp:collect all variable terms on one side]] and constant terms on the other using addition/subtraction.
Finally, [[imp:isolate the variable]] by multiplying or dividing. Remember to reverse the symbol if multiplying/dividing by a negative.

formulaCard.formula: $$ ax + b < cx + d \;\Rightarrow\; (a-c)x < d - b $$
notes: Collect variable terms on one side, constants on the other.
If $ a - c $ is negative, reverse the inequality when dividing.
formulaCard.title: Variables on Both Sides

teacherCues: Write '6x - 5 < 2x + 11' on the board. Ask: 'How is this similar to equations with variables on both sides?'
Guide students to add 5 and subtract 2x, just as they would with an equation.
Write '8b - 3 > 4(2b + 3)' on the board and simplify to '-3 > 12'. Ask: 'Is this ever true? What does that mean for the original inequality?'
Contrast with an identity like '2(5w - 1) ≤ 7 + 10w' simplifying to '-2 ≤ 7' (always true).

discoveryHook.scenario: Just like equations, some inequalities are always true, and some are never true. Recognizing these special cases saves you time and avoids frustration. If the variable disappears and leaves a true statement, every number works! If it leaves a false statement, no number works.

examples.title: A – No Solution
steps: Distribute: $ 8b - 3 > 8b + 12 $.
Subtract $ 8b $ from both sides: $ -3 > 12 $, which is false.
No solution.
Distribute: $ 10w - 2 \le 7 + 10w $.
Subtract $ 10w $: $ -2 \le 7 $, which is always true.
All real numbers are solutions.
examples.title: B – All Real Numbers
examples.peerPrompt: Explain to a partner: Why do we say all real numbers are solutions when we get $ -2 \le 7 $?

examples.prompt: Without solving completely, determine if $ 3(2a - 1) \ge 10a - 11 $ has a special solution.
steps: Distribute: $ 6a - 3 \ge 10a - 11 $.
Variable terms differ, so it's likely one solution or a range.
Solve: $ -3 \ge 4a - 11 $ → $ 8 \ge 4a $ → $ a \le 2 $. One range, not a special solution.
examples.title: C – Recognizing Before Solving

blocks.title: Special Solutions of Inequalities

questions.prompt: If simplifying an inequality leads to a false statement like $ -3 > 12 $, the inequality has ___ solution.
hints: It's the opposite of 'all real numbers'.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: Because $ -10 < 5 $ is always true, all real numbers are solutions.
questions.prompt: Solve $ 2(k - 5) < 2k + 5 $. How many solutions? (one word: none, one, or all)
What must be true about the variable terms on both sides for a 'special solution' (all real numbers or no solution) to occur?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The variable terms must be identical (or cancel completely).

confusionCorner.body: If the variable cancels and the inequality is true (like $ -2 \le 7 $), every real number works. If it's false (like $ -3 > 12 $), no number works. Always check the truth of the remaining statement.
confusionCorner.title: Don't Confuse No Solution with All Real Numbers

explanation: After simplifying and collecting variable terms, the variable may cancel out entirely.
If the resulting statement is [[imp:false]] (e.g., $ -3 > 12 $), the inequality has [[imp:no solution]].
If the resulting statement is [[imp:true]] (e.g., $ -2 \le 7 $), the inequality is an [[kw:identity]] and [[imp:all real numbers]] are solutions.
These special solutions happen when the variable expressions on each side are identical.

formulaCard.title: Identifying Special Solutions
notes: If $ b > c $ is true, all real numbers are solutions.
If $ b > c $ is false, no solution.

discoveryHook.scenario: Your trivia team needs an average of 90 to advance. After four games, your scores are 95, 91, 77, and 89. What do you need in the final game? A multi-step inequality will tell you exactly the minimum score required to keep your championship hopes alive!

examples.title: A – Advancing in Trivia
steps: Sum knowns: $ 352 + x $ over 5. Multiply by 5: $ 352 + x \ge 450 $.
Subtract 352: $ x \ge 98 $. You need at least 98 points.
examples.prompt: Scores: 95, 91, 77, 89. Need mean at least 90 in 5 games. What score x in the fifth game?

examples.title: B – What If the Target is 85?
examples.prompt: Same first four scores, but now you need a mean of at least 85. What score do you need?
steps: Inequality: $ \frac{352 + x}{5} \ge 85 $.
Multiply by 5: $ 352 + x \ge 425 $. Subtract 352: $ x \ge 73 $.
You need at least 73 points.
examples.peerPrompt: Explain to a partner: Why does the required score drop so much when the target mean is lower?

examples.prompt: Account has $500. Minimum balance must be $200. How many $20 bills can you withdraw?
steps: Let w = number of $20 bills. $ 500 - 20w \ge 200 $.
Subtract 500: $ -20w \ge -300 $. Divide by -20 and reverse: $ w \le 15 $.
You can withdraw at most 15 bills.
examples.title: C – Budget for Withdrawals

teacherCues: Pose the trivia game mean score problem: 'Scores: 95, 91, 77, 89. Need mean at least 90. What score in the 5th game?'
Guide: Write the mean formula as an inequality. Solve using multi-step techniques.
blocks.title: Real-Life Applications

questions.prompt: If your first four scores sum to 352 and you need a mean of at least 90 in 5 games, what is the minimum fifth score?

hints: $\ge$ is read as 'greater than or equal to'.
questions.prompt: In the withdrawal problem, the inequality $ 500 - 20w \ge 200 $ models the condition that the balance must be at ___ $200.
A woodworker wants to earn at least $25 per hour. Materials cost $125. Write an inequality for hours h if they want to earn at least $500 total profit.

confusionCorner.title: Direction of Inequality with Negative Coefficients
confusionCorner.body: In the withdrawal problem, after moving terms we had $ -20w \ge -300 $. Dividing by -20 reverses the symbol to $ \le $. Always check: does the answer make sense? If you withdraw 16 bills, balance = $500 - $320 = $180, below $200.

explanation: Many real-world scenarios require setting up an inequality, not an equation, especially when dealing with minimum or maximum thresholds.
Use the mean formula: $ \text{mean} = \frac{\text{sum of values}}{\text{number of values}} $.
Translate phrases like 'at least' to $ \ge $, and 'at most' to $ \le $.
Solve the inequality using multi-step methods, and interpret the answer in context.

notes: Multiply by the number of values $ n $.
Then subtract the sum of known scores.
formulaCard.title: Mean Inequality

examples.prompt: Use the blueprint to solve: Scores 95, 91, 77, 89; need mean ≥ 90 after 5th game.
examples.title: A – Mean Score Blueprint
steps: Understand: Mean = sum/5 ≥ 90. Unknown: 5th score x.
Conclude: Score at least 98. Check: if x=98, mean = (352+98)/5 = 450/5 = 90 exactly.

examples.title: B – Withdrawal Blueprint
steps: Understand: Let w = number of $20 bills. $ 500 - 20w \ge 200 $.
Solve: Subtract 500: $ -20w \ge -300 $. Divide by -20, reverse: $ w \le 15 $.
Conclude: At most 15 bills. Check: 15×20 = 300, balance = 200 (okay).
examples.prompt: Use the blueprint: $500 balance, min $200, withdraw $20 bills. How many?
examples.peerPrompt: Explain to a partner: Why does the inequality become $ w \le 15 $, and what does that mean for how many bills you can withdraw?

examples.title: C – Multi-Step with Variables on Both Sides
steps: Understand: Right side: $ 3w - 7 $. Inequality: $ 3w - 5 > 3w - 7 $.
Solve: Subtract $ 3w $: $ -5 > -7 $, always true.
Conclude: All real numbers. Any w works.

discoveryHook.scenario: Multi-step inequalities combine everything you've learned: simplifying, collecting terms, and watching for that negative flip. The blueprint helps you stay organized: Understand the situation, Solve step by step, and Conclude with the real-world meaning.

explanation: The blueprint for multi-step inequalities: [[imp:Understand]] the problem structure – identify the inequality symbol, any grouping symbols, and the variable's location.
[[imp:Solve]]: Simplify each side (distribute, combine), collect variable terms, isolate the variable. Reverse the symbol if multiplying/dividing by a negative.
[[imp:Conclude]]: Graph the solution and/or state the answer in the context of the problem. Check if the solution makes sense.

rows.1: Identify operations, inequality symbol, and any parentheses.
Simplify, collect terms, isolate variable (reverse symbol if ×/÷ by negative).
Graph solution; check in original inequality; answer in context.

formulaCard.title: Blueprint Summary
notes: Same as solving equations, but watch for negative multipliers/divisors.
Special solutions may appear if variables cancel.

confusionCorner.body: In real-life problems, 'no solution' means the requirement can never be met (e.g., need a score over 100 on a test where max is 100). 'All real numbers' means the condition is automatically satisfied regardless of the variable's value.
confusionCorner.title: No Solution vs. All Real Numbers in Context

blocks.title: Blueprint Aid – Multi-Step Inequalities
teacherCues: Display the Understand → Solve → Conclude framework. Walk through the trivia game problem using the blueprint.
Emphasize that 'Understand' includes identifying the mean formula and the inequality direction from 'at least'.

hints: It involves identifying the inequality and what is unknown.
questions.prompt: In the blueprint, what is the first phase?
During the Solve phase, if you divide by a ___ number, you must reverse the inequality symbol.
hints: This rule is unique to inequalities.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Divide by a negative number requires reversing the inequality symbol.

questions.answer: state all real numbers are solutions
hints: The inequality simplifies to a true statement.
You need to interpret that result.
questions.prompt: After solving $ 3w - 5 > 2w + w - 7 $, what do you do in the Conclude phase?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Conclude that all real numbers are solutions.

presenterNotes: Multi-step inequalities combine all previous inequality skills. Emphasize that the solving process mirrors multi-step equations, with one key addition: reversing the symbol when multiplying/dividing by a negative.
For special solutions, have students physically cross out the variable terms to see what remains. A true statement means every number works; a false statement means no number works.
In real-world problems, always check the reasonableness of the answer against the context. For mean problems, the required score must be possible (e.g., can't exceed 100 on a test).
